NDT training in Bath, Maine: how it works for Bath employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training for Bath-area employers and technicians, either as live online theory or onsite at your own facility, under ASNT Level III oversight. There is no Atlantis classroom building in Bath. Your employer's written practice decides what certification means, and a Level III gives the exams. Bath Iron Works' supply chain, Midcoast fabricators and marine repair shops use the training to qualify people in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT for work on naval hulls, welded structure and workboats.

Bath is a shipyard town, and inspection work here follows shipbuilding documentation. A technician on a destroyer hull block, a fabricator supplying outfitting steel, or a repair crew on a Casco Bay workboat all end up answering the same questions. Is the procedure qualified? Is the person certified to the employer's written practice for that method and level? Can the records stand up to a customer or government audit? The training below is built around those three questions, not around a generic textbook syllabus.

Most Bath-area demand comes from three kinds of employer. First, subcontractors and suppliers to the destroyer programme, who need technicians whose certification a prime contractor's quality team will accept. Second, general fabrication and machine shops across the Brunswick, Topsham, Lewiston-Auburn and Portland corridor that weld to AWS D1.1 or to a customer's own specification. Third, maintenance and reliability teams at Maine's pulp and paper mills, power stations and fuel terminals, who need thickness gauging, weld checks and pressure-equipment examinations. Each group starts in a different place, so we build the course plan around your scope instead of selling a fixed catalogue. Request a Bath training quote and describe the work your people inspect.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Bath

Every course follows the ASNT SNT-TC-1A recommended practice. Level I and Level II courses cover principles, equipment, calibration, technique and interpretation to an approved procedure. Level III preparation covers the Basic exam, method exams and the procedure-writing skills a Level III needs to run a programme. Training hours and experience for each method and level are listed in our training-requirements matrix. Your written practice may ask for more.

MethodLevelsWhat Bath-area employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (ultrasonic testing)I, II, III prepPlate lamination checks, full-penetration hull and structural welds, thickness surveys on tanks, digesters and marine structureHigh-school maths; Level I before Level II
PAUT (phased array UT)II, III prepFaster weld coverage on thick sections, encoded scans for traceable records, repair verificationConventional UT Level II recommended
TOFD (time-of-flight diffraction)II, III prepFlaw sizing on thick butt welds, pressure-equipment fabrication, pairing with PAUTConventional UT Level II recommended
RT (radiographic testing)I, II, III prepFilm and digital interpretation of butt welds, castings, piping spools; film reading for shop RTRadiation-safety training and state/federal requirements for anyone handling sources
MT (magnetic particle testing)I, II, III prepSurface and near-surface cracks in ferritic hull steel, fillet welds, lifting gear, machined partsVision test; no method prerequisite
PT (liquid penetrant testing)I, II, III prepNon-magnetic materials: stainless piping, aluminium superstructure, castings, machined aerospace-supply partsVision test; no method prerequisite
VT (visual testing)I, II, III prepFit-up, weld profile and workmanship checks, corrosion and coating surveys, the first gate before any volumetric methodVision test
ET (eddy current testing)I, II, III prepHeat-exchanger and condenser tubing, surface cracks in aluminium and coated parts, conductivity checksBasic electrical knowledge helpful

A typical Midcoast technician starts in VT, MT and PT, which are the methods used most on welded steel. UT is added next, then PAUT or RT depending on what the employer needs. Level III candidates usually hold several Level II certifications and want structured preparation for the Basic and method exams. Our ASNT Level III training covers that path.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Bath, step by step

  1. Employer written practice. Under SNT-TC-1A, the employer certifies its own people. The written practice sets training hours, experience, exam content, passing grades and recertification intervals for each method and level. If your Bath shop doesn't have one yet, that comes first.
  2. Formal classroom training. The candidate completes the method-and-level training hours required by the written practice, online or onsite. See the requirements matrix for recommended minimums.
  3. On-the-job experience. The candidate works under certified personnel on real work and logs the hours. On a shipyard or fabrication floor, that means documented time on the welds and parts the certification will cover.
  4. General examination. A written exam on method principles, administered under the authority of a Level III.
  5. Specific examination. A written exam on the employer's procedures, equipment, codes and acceptance criteria, for example the customer specification your shop inspects to.
  6. Practical examination. Hands-on testing of real specimens with known flaws. The candidate calibrates, examines, records and evaluates to procedure while a Level III watches.
  7. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast checks, repeated every year.
  8. Certification. The employer's Level III and responsible manager sign the certification. It is valid only for that employer.
  9. Recertification. At the interval in the written practice, by examination or by evidence of continuing satisfactory performance, whichever the practice allows.

For more detail on how the employer-based model works, read our SNT-TC-1A training and certification guide.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Bath crews

We deliver three ways, and none of them assumes a training centre in Bath, because we don't have one.

  • Live online theory. Instructor-led sessions for the classroom part of Level I and Level II. This suits technicians on shift, or small shops that can't release several people at once. See online NDT training for the format.
  • Onsite at your facility. An instructor comes to your shop, yard office or plant and teaches on your own equipment, procedures and reference standards. Practical exams can be given there under Level III oversight. For a Bath-area fabricator, this means crews train on the joint types and materials they actually inspect.
  • Blended. Theory online first, then a short, focused onsite block for practical work and exams.

Scheduling matters in a shipbuilding economy. Production milestones, hull moves and customer inspections set the calendar, and nobody wants inspectors in a classroom during a critical module test. We plan onsite blocks around your production schedule and around planned mill outages or shutdowns for paper and power clients. Cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day. Ask about onsite training for your Bath crew.

Where NDT technicians work in Bath

Naval shipbuilding. Bath Iron Works builds Arleigh Burke-class destroyers, and the whole local industrial base grows around it. Naval surface-ship work uses NAVSEA technical publications for inspection. These include the NAVSEA NDT requirements publication (T9074-AS-GIB-010/271) and MIL-STD-2035 acceptance criteria, used alongside the prime contractor's own qualification rules. Suppliers usually find the prime has its own personnel-approval steps on top of SNT-TC-1A certification. Our training builds the method competence and paperwork those steps rely on. It does not replace the prime's own approval.

Submarine maintenance. Portsmouth Naval Shipyard in Kittery, about an hour south, brings nuclear-submarine overhaul work into southern Maine. Navy nuclear and security rules apply there, and they are separate from commercial certification.

Fabrication and construction. Structural and module fabricators across Maine weld to AWS D1.1 and to project specifications. That keeps VT, MT and UT in steady demand. Bridge work for the Maine DOT and port and pier projects on the coast add structural-steel inspection.

Pulp, paper and energy. Maine's paper mills run recovery boilers, digesters and pressure vessels that need thickness surveys and weld checks at every outage. Biomass and gas-fired power plants add boiler-tube and piping scopes. Fuel terminals on the Portland waterfront need tank and piping inspection.

Legacy nuclear. Maine Yankee in nearby Wiscasset was decommissioned. Its independent spent-fuel storage installation remains, and its work follows nuclear quality-assurance programmes.

Radiography licensing in Maine. Maine is an NRC Agreement State. The Maine CDC Radiation Control Program licenses radioactive materials, including the gamma sources used in industrial radiography, and registers X-ray equipment. Anyone who works as an industrial radiographer or radiographer's assistant has to meet the licensee's radiation-safety training and certification requirements, which are separate from ASNT method certification. Work in areas of exclusive federal jurisdiction, such as some Navy sites, may fall under NRC or Navy rules instead. Your radiation safety officer confirms which rules apply to a given job. Our RT course teaches interpretation and technique. It does not issue a radiographer licence.

What local employers ask for. Hiring managers in the Bath-Brunswick area usually want SNT-TC-1A certification in at least two methods, clean training and experience records, and familiarity with the codes they inspect to. Some also ask for AWS welding-inspector credentials or other schemes. Atlantis doesn't train for those. We cover the ASNT method side.

Level III services and written practices for Bath NDT companies

Many small Maine shops don't employ a full-time Level III, and some still inspect without a written practice that would hold up in an audit. Both problems come up quickly when a prime contractor, a navy customer or an ISO 9001 auditor asks for the paperwork. Atlantis provides:

  • Written-practice development. A practice written to SNT-TC-1A for your methods and levels, set up for how your shop actually works. See written-practice development.
  • Outside Level III services. Exam administration, procedure review and technique sheets, and records audits under your programme.
  • Corporate programmes. Multi-person, multi-method training plans with a certification tracker. See corporate NDT training.

Book a Level III consultation to review your current practice and find the gaps before your customer does.

Practise before the practical exam

Most candidates fail the practical exam on technique, not theory. Our Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. Technicians can repeat set-up, scanning and indication evaluation as often as they want before exam day. It is only for practice. The practical exam is still done on real specimens with a real instrument, in front of a Level III.

Your instructor

The lead instructor is Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He designs the course content, supervises the programmes and gives the Level III oversight behind the exams.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Bath

How do I get NDT certified in Bath, Maine?

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you by following its written practice. You complete the classroom training, log on-the-job experience, pass the general, specific and practical exams given under a Level III, and pass a vision test. If you are not employed yet, you can do the formal training now. Certification comes once an employer takes you on and signs it off.

Can I take NDT training online in Maine?

Yes, the theory part. Live online classes cover the classroom hours for Level I and Level II and Level III exam preparation. The practical part has to be done hands-on with real equipment and specimens, and we can arrange that onsite at your employer's facility.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on the classroom hours and experience your employer's written practice requires. Most practices follow the SNT-TC-1A recommended minimums, which are listed in our training-requirements matrix. Classroom time is short compared with the logged field experience, which usually sets the overall timeline.

Do I need a license for radiography in Maine?

Radiographic work with radioactive sources has to be done under a radioactive materials licence. Maine is an Agreement State, so the Maine CDC Radiation Control Program issues that licence. Individual radiographers must meet the licensee's radiation-safety training and certification rules. ASNT RT certification covers technique and interpretation, not the radiation-safety licence.

What does NDT training cost in Bath?

We don't publish fixed prices. The cost depends on the methods, the levels, the group size and whether the training is online or onsite. Send your requirements and we'll return a cohort or onsite quote within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Bath employers?

SNT-TC-1A is the usual basis for NDT personnel qualification in US shipbuilding, fabrication and energy work. Naval programmes add their own rules and approval steps on top, so the employer's written practice and the customer's specification decide exactly what is accepted.

Do I need welding experience before NDT training?

No, but it helps a lot on the Bath waterfront. Technicians who understand joint design, welding processes and typical defects learn VT, MT and UT faster and interpret indications with more confidence.

Which NDT method should I learn first to work in shipbuilding?

VT, MT and PT are the usual starting methods on welded steel, followed by UT. Radiography and phased array come later, based on what your employer needs.

Can my Bath shop run the exams onsite?

Yes. Under an SNT-TC-1A programme, a Level III can give the general, specific and practical exams at your facility using your procedures and specimens, as your written practice sets out.

Does Atlantis offer AWS or API inspector courses?

No. Our training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A method training only. Some local employers also ask for other credentials, and candidates earn those separately through the bodies that issue them.

What do NDT technicians earn in Maine?

Pay depends on level, methods, clearances and overtime. Our NDT salary guide summarises published ranges instead of quoting unverified local figures.

Are there practice questions for the UT Level II exam?

Yes. Start with our UT Level II practice questions, then use the Practical NDT simulator to rehearse technique.
